title: Reverse-Seared Rib-Eye Steak with Thyme and Garlic
summary: Thick rib-eye steaks are slow-roasted at a low oven heat, then finished in a smoking-hot pan with butter, garlic and thyme for an even cook and a dark, savoury crust.
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray
heavy cast-iron or carbon-steel frying pan (28 cm)

ingredients.item: thick rib-eye steaks (4-5 cm thick, about 500 g each)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Dry and season
steps.text: Pat the steaks completely dry and season every surface with the salt and pepper. If time allows, leave them uncovered on the rack in the fridge for 1-24 h, then take them out 30 min before cooking. A drier surface browns far faster in the pan, so the crust forms before the inside overcooks.

steps.title: Slow roast
steps.text: Heat the oven to 120°C (fan 100°C) and roast the steaks on the rack in the tray for 35-55 min, until a thermometer pushed into the centre of each reads 54°C. This is only a halfway mark, because the sear will finish the cooking. Trust the thermometer rather than the clock, as thickness and starting temperature vary.

steps.title: Brief rest
steps.text: Leave the steaks on the rack for 10 min. During this pause the surface cools and dries a little more, which helps the pan sear quickly and cleanly.

steps.title: Sear hard and fast
steps.text: Set the pan over high heat until it just begins to smoke, add the oil and lay in the steaks. Sear for 1-1.5 min per side until deeply browned, then stand them on their fat edge for 1 min to render it. Very high heat gives a rich crust in seconds, so the gently cooked centre is left undisturbed.

steps.title: Baste with butter
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium and add the butter, garlic and thyme. Once the butter foams, tilt the pan and spoon it over the steaks for 1 min; the milk solids brown and carry the garlic and herb flavour onto the crust.

steps.title: Check and slice
steps.text: Probe the centre of each steak: it must read at least 63°C. If it falls short, keep basting over medium heat and check every 30 s. Rest on the board for 3 min, then slice across the grain and spoon the pan butter, garlic and thyme over the top.

tips: A common mistake is skipping the thermometer and relying on cooking times; steak thickness varies so much that only the probe reading is reliable.
Start with properly thick steaks of 4-5 cm, because thin ones overcook in the oven before the sear even starts.
Make sure the pan is genuinely smoking before the steaks go in, otherwise they steam and turn grey instead of browning.
Squeeze the soft roasted garlic out of its skins and spread it over the sliced steak.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours and refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently until piping hot (74°C), or slice cold for sandwiches and salads.
